text: The transaction stream comes in through an Eventstream, the same mechanism Fabric taught for dashboards. Here the consumer computes features from the stream as it flows, because scoring needs them within a sub-second budget.

A fraud signal like five purchases in two minutes is a rolling count over a moving interval — that points to a sliding window, not a tumbling one, which would split a burst across a boundary and undercount it.

The features a fraud model needs are rolling aggregates per card — count and sum over a sliding window, not the whole table. Each new feature record is what gets handed to scoring; the model never sees raw transactions.

A late transaction either gets dropped or triggers a recomputation. A watermark decides how long to wait for late data — too short excludes real transactions, too long misses the latency budget. No universal right answer.
Ingestion and features are flowing, on the right window shape, with a deliberate watermark trade-off. Next up: turning those features into an actual score, and alerting without double-counting.
